It featured gaming mechanics in which you need to bounce a ball through many different three-dimensional textured tubes, to collect as many points as you can while trying not to fall off the edge.
The creator Kefir_Union has said there are a number of differences compared to the Atari version of Yoomp. As in Jump! there are 16 tiles on an axis game field, there are 10 deep tiles that are visible instead of 4 for better planning of moment, newly added special orange bonus fields, which change game for collecting points, there are more special fields which may cause other fields to disappear, the game will have 28 levels of challenging ball bouncing fun, 5 music tracks by XTD/Lamers, and playable in a resolution 320x256 in 256 colours!

423038.overview: A Licenseware game created by Sparx in 1991. A jigsaw puzzle game created using high quality picture scans. The game would allow you to create your own puzzles or play the many included puzzles, it also had children and adult difficulty levels. At least 3 freeware puzzle packs were created for the game, the first by Sparx itself and later ones by Jim Campey.

423054.overview: A casino style blackjack simulator created by Jack Prichard with AMOS and sold as shareware beginning in 1992. Has the ability to double or split, insurance and helpful betting and playing info as well as the ability to change cards.

423055.overview: An AMOS based shareware game published by Cellblock4 in 1997. Jet Set Willy '97 is an unofficial sequel/reboot of the original 1984 Jet Set Willy. The game is a platformer where your goal is to collect a large number of items scattered across many rooms. Each room takes up one screen, and has a unique name. You can travel from one room to an adjacent room by walking, jumping or falling off the edge of the screen. The items that you need to collect are identified by changing color rapidly -- there are other objects that are just part of the background and can be ignored. There are also many patrolling enemies that can kill you. Some platforms are conveyor belts that will push you in one direction when you stand on them, and there are staircases (diagonal lines of pixels) that let you reach higher platforms.

423060.overview: A Czech language text adventure from Kamil Blazek in 1990. It is a remake of the multiple choice text adventure from Atari based on a famous movie or the novel by Eco. The story is said to be based on a true event that happened at the Melk Monastery in Northern Italy. The task is to catch the murderer of the slain monks in the act. As for the game mechanics, this is not a classic text book, but rather an interactive novel, where we always read the text and choose one of the three continuation options based on it.

423293.overview: A homebrew game by Jean Pierre Software, a sides-scrolling football\soccer game for one player. Kick football, get check, repeat.

423392.overview: Manage the Pope, help him successfully skydive into heavily defended military installations. The title was intended for you to confuse this as being a Jeanie-Pierre Papin soccer manager, he being an Italian player for AC Milan, but instead you control Pape, aka The Pope. He has his own Popemobile, and that is cool, he also likes to skydive apparently!

423536.overview: A quite well known and nicely made turn based role-playing game set in the land of Cordovan. As Member of the Adventurer Guild take the challenge on your own, the seven magical jewels have been divided by evil forces and the country no longer protected.  As expected, the player is able to adventure with the most diverse characters supported to choose from. Find the precious stones in imaginative adventures  set in an open world. Friends of this genre will enjoy hours and days of play.

423751.overview:
A homebrew port of the game from Hot Software in 1990. Jack the Nipper is a platform game that contains 50 screens packed with action.

Jack is an evil and wicked toddler. You play Jack and you have to cause as much trouble without being penalized for it. To see how naughty you've been there is a naughtyometer at the bottom of the screen.

To cause some mayhem Jack must jump on things, pick up objects and drop those at places where they cause the most trouble to grown-ups.

The various objects can be found all over town and at Jack's home. The game starts at Jack's home but Jack can walk out the door and go into town to, for example, blow up the police station, kill all flowers or free prisoners. Try to get a credit card and do some serious shopping!

The first thing you should look for is you peashooter and fire peas at various objects or persons. Toot your horn to frustrate grown-ups or animals.

The naughtier your the higher your naughtyometer goes up! The game comes to an end as the naughtyometer reaches 100%. Cause as much trouble as you can... but don't get spanked for it by grown-ups!

440402.overview: Jump N Bump is a cute but gory four player action game, originally created by Brainchild Design in 1998, now it's available on Amiga

449074.overview:
Jungle Boy is an arcade game heavily inspired by Taitos arcade Jungle King from 1982.

There are four levels with different tasks. In the first level you have to jump from liana to liana, which are swinging and you have to press the joystick button at time to jump. The second level is avoid getting eaten by crocodiles in a river by moving up and down. In the next level two levels animals and cannibals are coming for you and you have to stay alive by jumping over them.

The levels are scrolling horizontally from left to right. The levels are very short and playing through the game only takes some minutes.

452151.overview: Jolly Royal is a video poker game for the Commodore Amiga. It was developed by Michael Greifenhahn and released into the public domain in 1992.

461182.overview: It's Jurl, the Asteroids meets Pacman game where you have to collect all the space diamonds whilst avoiding the various aliens.

480307.overview: Langford Productions' Jetpac remake, HD art and all, running natively on a 68040 Amiga.

482506.overview: An unofficial port of Taito’s 1982 arcade game Jungle King, made by static recompilation: the arcade’s two Z80 programs are translated into native 68020 code. It is not an emulator.
